claims: The `--quota-floor` stop goes stale when Arkham sends no Remaining header (`tier1-bulk-enrich.mjs:541-546`, `:1000`, `:1058`): `quota.remaining` is only set when `/subscription/intel-usage` is polled and is never recalculated from Usage/Limit headers, so the check at `:1000` compares against an old number and the stop can't fire for up to 500 lookups

`--limit` with no value silently removes the cap (`tier1-bulk-enrich.mjs:112-117`, `:126`): `--limit --quota-floor 50` or `--limit` as the last argument returns `undefined`, so the limit becomes `Infinity` and the whole ~68k queue runs
`--chain` with no value quietly becomes `"all"`, which points resume at the wrong progress file

Tier-2's forensic tags are still dropped in the final label write (`tier2-light-forensic.mjs:672-682`): `mergedTags` puts `existingEntry.tags` first, then `derived.tags`, then keeps only the first 20, so `entity:`, `slug:`, `ctp:` and `type:contract` tags are cut off

Refresh merges drop tier-2 and human-added tags (`tier1-bulk-enrich.mjs:726-728`, and `src/lib/arkham.ts:374-376` `mergeRefreshEntry`): fresh Arkham tags are put first, then existing tags, then only the first 20 are kept, so tags added by tier 2 or a person are deleted, including by the production refresh cron
A truncated discovery source only logs a warning (`tier1-bulk-enrich.mjs:284-288`): when a source hits `HARD_PAGE_CAP` it isn't added to `failedSources`, so the run goes ahead on a truncated set

Addresses that error before a circuit-breaker halt are never retried (`tier1-bulk-enrich.mjs:1043-1047`, `:966`, `:804-813`): error lines in the progress file carry `address` and resume treats every such address as done, so each trip of the 10-error breaker permanently skips those addresses

judge_reasoning.3845594538: The review never covers flushWrites splicing the pending batch before the pipeline call, which loses writes on a transient failure. Finding 6 concerns error lines in the progress file, a different problem.
judge_reasoning.3845596185: Finding 5 matches: a source that hits HARD_PAGE_CAP isn't added to failedSources, so the run goes ahead on a truncated set.
judge_reasoning.3845603922: The review doesn't mention the run.sh tfvars key prefix-matching bug. It even clears run.sh.
judge_reasoning.3845603940: The review looks at sanitizeEntry's cut-to-20-then-dedup order and clears it as a correct mirror, so it doesn't flag this defect.
judge_reasoning.3845607361: Finding 3 matches: tier2's mergedTags puts existingEntry.tags first and keeps only 20, so ctp:/type: forensic tags get dropped.
judge_reasoning.3845618202: Finding 4 matches: refresh merges put fresh Arkham tags first and slice to 20, which wipes tier-2 forensic tags.

1.why: noteQuotaHeaders (l.531-549) sets quota.remaining only from a Remaining header and never computes limit-usage. With no Remaining header, the only other source is logIntelUsage, which runs every INTEL_USAGE_EVERY=500 addresses (l.1060), so the floor check at l.1000 uses a number up to 500 lookups old.

2.why: flagValue returns undefined when the next arg is missing or starts with '--' (l.112-117), and numericFlag then returns the Infinity fallback (l.126), so a bare --limit slips past the hard-fail check that was added for bad values and the cap is gone (l.855).

3.why: The base script exited when --chain had no value. Now flagValue returns undefined, so scope becomes 'all' (l.135) and the run silently uses tier1-progress-all.jsonl (l.801) instead of the chain's progress file.

4.why: Number('') is 0, so the limit is 0 and nothing gets processed. That fails safe and the claim names no harm.

5.why: Same as known tier2-light-forensic.mjs:395 'Preserve Tier 2 tags when merging capped labels'. mergedTags puts existing tags first and then applies slice(0,20).

6.why: Same as known tier1-bulk-enrich.mjs:774 'Refresh wipes forensic tags'. buildWriteEntry and mergeRefreshEntry put fresh tags first, then sanitize and cap.

7.why: Same as known tier1:328 / tier1:311 HARD_PAGE_CAP findings. A capped source only gets a log suffix (l.284-288) and is never added to failedSources.

8.why: Error lines are written as {address,error} (l.1043-1047), and resume adds every line's address to processed (l.805-813). The new breaker exits(3) and says the progress file 'resumes the queue' (l.966), but those errored addresses are skipped for good.
